stem: Which infant has the highest baseline risk of cryptorchidism?

options.text: A term infant with normal birth weight and no relevant family history
A premature infant with low birth weight
A term infant whose mother had an uncomplicated pregnancy and no smoking history
A term infant with normal birth weight born after spontaneous conception
A term infant with no family history and no maternal metabolic risk factors

explanation: Prematurity with low birth weight is the strongest baseline risk profile for cryptorchidism.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because this profile does not include the key risk factors associated with cryptorchidism.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because prematurity and low birth weight are recognised risk factors for cryptorchidism, making this infant the highest risk option.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because an uncomplicated pregnancy and no smoking history do not increase baseline risk in the way prematurity and low birth weight do.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because term birth with normal birth weight does not suggest the increased risk seen with prematurity and low birth weight.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the absence of family history and maternal metabolic risk factors does not identify the main recognised risk factors for cryptorchidism.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
